title: InterSystems IRIS Overview
description: Overview of InterSystems IRIS instance health, high availability (mirroring), Enterprise Cache Protocol (ECP) distributed caching, interoperability, and logs. Mirror, ECP, and outbound HTTP widgets show "No data" on deployments that do not use those features.

definition.content:
InterSystems IRIS is a data platform combining a multi-model database, interoperability engine, and analytics runtime. This dashboard tracks instance health, high availability (mirroring), Enterprise Cache Protocol (ECP) distributed caching, and interoperability productions.

- **Mirror**, **ECP**, and **outbound HTTP** widgets show *No data* when those features are not in use; this is expected.
- Event-style signals (failovers, process termination, license warnings) surface in the **Logs** group, which parses both `messages.log` and `structured.log`.

**Useful links:**
- [Datadog InterSystems IRIS integration documentation](https://docs.datadoghq.com/integrations/intersystems_iris/)
- [InterSystems IRIS product documentation](https://docs.intersystems.com/)

Instance-wide health and the state of this integration's monitors. **System state:** -1 hung, 0 OK, 1 warning, 2 alert. **Mirror status:** 1 not initialized, 2 primary, 3 backup, 4 connected, 5 transition, 6 synchronizing, 7 waiting, 8 stopped, 9 crashed.
Storage and daemon headroom on the instance. **Write daemon:** 0 active, 1 suspended. Lock table fullness is derived from the shared-memory `Lock_Table` gauge.
CPU, memory, license consumption, cache efficiency, and write and journal daemon activity over time.
Mirror member roles, synchronization status, failover readiness, and backup replication lag. Shows no data on deployments that do not use mirroring.

formulas.alias: Status (2 Pri/3 Bkp/5 Trans/8 Stop/9 Crash)

definition.title: Mirror members: role, sync status, and readiness (per host)

definition.content: Enterprise Cache Protocol connections. An instance usually acts as either an application server (client) or a data server, so expect only one set of widgets to report. Shows no data when ECP is not in use.
Business host status, message throughput, error and abort counts, and queue depth across interoperability productions.

definition.title: Business hosts: activity and message counts (per business host)
Errors, aborts, discards, and suspends (new per interval, per production)
Queue depth by production over time
Outbound HTTP and SOAP latency (per business host; appears only with live outbound traffic)
